variants.name: Hand-rolled binary heap with an index map
variants.idiom_name: binary heap plus an unordered_map from key to position
variants.implementation_notes: The variant needed when the algorithm requires decrease-key or removal-by-key (Dijkstra with a real frontier). Every swap updates the index map, which turns an O(n) search-and-remove into an O(log n) sift. More code, more to test, and the invariant check is the same: one linear scan comparing children to parents.
variants.code_sketch:
// swap(i, j) must also do pos_[a[i].key] = i; pos_[a[j].key] = j;
// decrease_key(k, p) { int i = pos_[k]; heap_[i].p = p; sift_up(i); sift_down(i); }
pitfalls: Forgetting to update the index on every swap is the classic bug and the failure is intermittent.
The map must be updated in sift-up AND sift-down AND pop, which is every code path.
